title: Length-Latency Tradeoff Mapper & Prefill Scheduling—kernel adaptor
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: This ticket designs and lands a Length-Latency Tradeoff Mapper (LLTM) that maps incoming requests' sequence-length and latency SLO profile to a small set of bucket/slot configurations and a kernel-adaptor hint. The mapper's goal is to reduce padding overhead across prefill and decode phases while preserving 95th percentile latency targets. The design couples three levers: (1) lightweight per-request length profiling at admission, (2) runtime bucket assignment that considers kernel affinity (sparse vs dense attention kernels, quantized kernel capabilities), and (3) prefill-aware scheduling which gives prefill requests prioritized packing to maximize KV cache reuse and avoid decode tail amplification.

Background & motivation: We repeatedly observe token inflation from conservative fixed-length buckets: short prefill requests get padded to mid-sized chunks and suffer unnecessary compute and memory overhead. Meanwhile, decode latency tails worsen when mixed-length groups are decoded with kernels that have suboptimal sequence-length throughput. Prior work (see ENG-4721, ENG-11356) reduced padding using histograms and bucketing, but kernel-level affinity and prefill/decode phase separation were not first-class. This ticket aims to close that gap.

Goals:
- Reduce mean token-padding by >= 18% for typical conversational workloads (bench: ChatFlow synthetic trace) without regressing p95 latency beyond 5% for P50 latency target customers.
- Improve kernel utilization by introducing a kernel-hint field that leads runtime to choose the best-attention kernel and quantized path when applicable.
- Ensure prefill scheduling reuses KV cache for subsequent decodes when requests are part of an apparent multi-turn session (heuristics + short session affinity IDs).

Design overview:
1) Admission sampler: At request arrival, compute a fast length fingerprint (prefill vs decode flag, input token count, estimated response token budget). Use this as input to LLTM.
2) LLTM: A rule+ML hybrid where rules handle obvious cases (very short <= 16, very long >= 1024) and a lightweight logistic model maps length+client-slo to a bucket id and kernel-hint. Bucket id includes target slot size and allowed padding budget.
3) Kernel adaptor hint: runtime accepts the hint in the serve RPC. Hints: "dense-opt", "sparse-opt", "quant4a-opt", "fallback". Runtime still validates compatibility (model/quantization) and can override on resource constraints.
4) Prefill-aware scheduler: Prefills with high session-affinity score get assigned packing priority to be placed in slots that maximize KV cache locality and avoid interleaving with long decode-only streams. Prefill priority is limited to avoid starvation (weighted fairness).
5) Telemetry & learning loop: Track pad ratio, p50/p95 latency per bucket+kernel hint, and an online EWMA that flips rule thresholds if pad savings and latency meet targets for 1 hour window. Send aggregated metrics to Console for visibility.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated canary: deploy LLTM behind a feature flag, route 10% of traffic; must show pad reduction >= 12% and no p95 latency regression > 5% across 6-hour window before scaling to 50%.
- Kernel hinting must not increase model error rate (log-prob delta) beyond 0.2% in eval prompts. CI will run 100 eval prompts comparing outputs.
- Prefill scheduler must improve KV cache hit-rate in controlled testbench by >= 20% for multi-turn sessions.

Implementation notes & trade-offs:
- We choose a small hybrid model (5–10 input features) for latency predictability; a larger model would be more accurate but harder to run atomically at admission.
- Kernel hints are advisory. In overloaded conditions, runtime override avoids capacity-induced slowdowns; we log overrides to root-cause mismatches.
- Prefill prioritization improves cache reuse but risks increased queuing for low-priority decode-only workloads; we implement weighted fairness tokens to throttle prioritization.

Testing plan:
- Microbench: synthetic traces (ChatFlow, SearchAssist) across sequence-length distributions; measure pad ratio, throughput, latency percentiles.
- Load test: run canary on dedicated pool with fault injection to exercise runtime overrides; collect kernel selection histograms.
- Quality check: run eval set to ensure no semantic regressions when selecting different kernels.

Rollout & monitoring:
- Rollout steps: feature-flag 10% (6h), 50% (24h), 100% (72h) with automatic rollback if p95 regresses > 7% or pad ratio worsens.
- Dashboards: per-bucket pad ratio, kernel-hint distribution, p50/p95, KV cache hit-rate, override rate.

Follow-ups (if successful):
- Tighten bucket granularity for long-tail sequences and introduce per-customer learned adjustments.
- Expose a Console toggle to bias towards cost or latency for specific routes.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/LLTM+Design
- PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7821
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/runtime/lltm-prefill-canary

Risks:
- Misclassification increases tail latency if kernel hint is repeatedly overridden; mitigated by logging and runtime override thresholds.
- Small admission model could drift; mitigation: daily retrain job using sampled traffic and safe rollout with shadow-testing.

2026-03-04 - Miguel Ortega: Spike results: packing priority increases KV cache hit-rate from 42% -> 62% on synthetic multi-turn testbench. Noted increased 95th latency for some decode-only streams; added weighted fairness to scheduler design.

2026-03-06 - Riley Kapoor (SRE): Observability hooks added to feature branch. We need to ensure logs for kernel-adaptor overrides are sampled — added proposal to cap sampling at 1% by default to limit cardinality.
2026-03-08 - Priya Nair (PM): Approved prioritization tradeoffs for release to canary. Requested a Console view showing per-customer pad changes and cost delta estimate for finance review.
2026-03-09 - Miguel Ortega: PR #7821 opened (draft). Unit tests for LLTM mapping logic added. Integration tests still pending for KV cache affinity behavior in the prefill scheduler.

2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Canary started at 10% traffic in a dedicated runtime slice. Early telemetry (3h): pad ratio -13%, p95 latency +1.8% (within threshold). Continuing to 6h window per acceptance criteria.
